record.title: Air Security reports a plugin SHA-pin checkout bypass in four coding agents
record.summary: Air Security’s September 17 disclosure describes Plugin4Shell, a reported Git checkout ambiguity that can defeat plugin commit pinning if a coding agent does not verify the resulting HEAD. Its authors say they built working PoCs against Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot and Gemini CLI. They report fixes in Claude Code 2.1.179 and Codex 0.146.0, no Copilot fix at disclosure, and no planned Gemini CLI fix after deprecation. The disclosure includes technical detail, but its exploit and product-status claims remain first-party and unreproduced here; it also has a commercial interest in agent supply-chain security. No real-world exploitation or affected-population estimate is established.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Air Security published a dated technical disclosure on 2026-09-17 and states that its lab built working proof-of-concept exploits against Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot and Gemini CLI. This establishes what the report says, not independent confirmation of the exploits.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Air Security reports that the named agents fail to verify that a Git checkout landed on the pinned commit; it describes a SHA-shaped branch/ref resolution path for Claude Code, Codex and Copilot, and a FETCH_HEAD name-resolution path for Gemini CLI.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The report says Claude Code 2.1.179 and Codex 0.146.0 contain fixes, GitHub Copilot had no shipped fix at disclosure, and Google would not patch the deprecated Gemini CLI. These status statements were not independently checked against vendor advisories in this activation.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of the SHA-shaped branch or FETCH_HEAD checkout paths was performed.
Fix, no-fix and deprecation statements are from the discloser; corresponding vendor advisories/release notes were not checked.
No real-world exploitation or affected-user measurement is established by the inspected disclosure.

brief.importance_rationale: If the described flaw is present in widely deployed coding agents, it can let control of an installed plugin repository substitute code despite a pinned commit, creating a consequential software supply-chain path into developer environments. The disclosure reports PoCs against four products, but no independent reproduction, vendor confirmation, exploitation evidence or affected-population estimate was established here.
limitations: The technical account and PoC scope come from the disclosing security vendor; no independent reproduction was recovered in this activation.
No vendor confirmation or independent version/advisory check was completed here.
Air Security sells agent supply-chain products; its claims about affected population, severity and its own product exemptions are not independently accepted.
No real-world exploitation, victim count or measured organizational impact is demonstrated.

technical.claimed_result: Air Security reports working PoCs for a plugin SHA-pin checkout bypass affecting four coding-agent products, with two claimed fixes and two products reported unresolved/deprecated at disclosure.
technical.demonstrated_result: The dated primary disclosure and its technical description are accessible. This activation verified the contents of the report, not the exploit against the products.
technical.mechanism: The report says the agent requests a pinned Git identifier but fails to check the resolved HEAD. It describes a hash-shaped branch taking precedence over a commit object in three products and a FETCH_HEAD-named default branch path in Gemini CLI.
technical.regime: The report concerns plugin installation/update paths in the named product versions and Git hosting configurations described by Air Security. The disclosure does not establish every configuration or current product status.
technical.reproducibility: Air Security says its lab built PoCs against four agents. No independent reproduction was done in this activation; a safe toy-Git reproduction and vendor-version checks remain open.
technical.strongest_baseline: Post-checkout validation of resolved HEAD against the requested pinned commit is the direct control described by the report; exact product fixes require vendor artifact inspection.

brief.title: Air Security reports a plugin SHA-pin checkout bypass in four coding agents
brief.why_it_matters: Commit pinning is often treated as proof that reviewed plugin code is what an agent executes. If the reported checkout behavior holds, the agent must verify the resolved working-tree commit itself; a marketplace pin alone would not establish that guarantee.
